tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

mnist-first-four-classes-setup: Section 3.1, p.6: the paper states the four-class MNIST subset and the reason (classes match qubits).
four-qubit-vqc-depth-one-to-six-setup: Section 4.1, p.7: 4-qubit VQC fixed, depth 1 to 6 layers, stated as the paper's own protocol.
model-selection-threshold-eighty-percent: Section 3.4, p.7: the paper states its own selection rule (noise-free accuracy above 80%).
noise-injection-placement-and-probabilit: Sections 3.5 and 3.5.1, p.7: noise gates placed before measurement, probabilities 0.1 to 1.0 step 0.1, five gate types, PennyLane. All stated as setup.
shots-fixed-no-statistical-noise-scope: Section 3.5.1, p.7: 1024 shots fixed and shot noise explicitly not studied.
qtl-resnet18-vqc-final-layer-setup: Section 2.3, p.4: 'we employ the pre-trained ResNet-18 ... augmented with a VQC serving as the final layer'.
qtl-excluded-from-noise-analysis-scope: Section 4.1, p.8: states that the noise analysis covers only QCNN and QuanNN, and why. The value states the scope decision.
best-configs-table-one-setup: Table 1, p.9: QCNN Strongly Entangling, 3 layers; QuanNN Basic Entangling, 3 layers. Section 4.1 says these are the only configurations carried into noise analysis.
egoqgnn-lemma2-linearly-dependent-states: Lemma 2, Section 4.1, p.5; proof in Appendix p.12: unit norm of A and B gives k squared = 1. The proof is complete for real k, the condition the second quote carries. The main-text statement omits 'k real'; the proof states it.
egoqgnn-ego-graph-definition-and-decompo: Section 4.4, p.6: 'we regard a node and its neighbors as an ego-graph'; N nodes give N ego-graphs, processed sequentially, merged classically. Section 1 gives the ego-graph definition.
egoqgnn-graph-representation-von-neumann: Section 4.5, p.7, Eq. 17-18: graph representation is the sum over nodes of von Neumann entropy of the pure node states.
egoqgnn-classification-rule-two-class-st: Section 4.5, p.7, Eq. 19: two reference states for the two classes (upper and lower Bloch hemispheres). The QSVM remark is the authors' own comparison; the rule is the definition.
egoqgnn-trainable-mapping-loss-definitio: Section 4.3, p.6-7, Eq. 13: loss over normalized Euclidean distances and normalized arccos distances between states; stated aim is to keep distance relations.
egoqgnn-three-bit-error-correction-inclu: Section 4.2, p.6, Fig. 2: the circuit uses the three-bit code of [45] with copy (UC) and recovery (UP) modules around the Ulayer.
egoqgnn-simulation-only-reason: Section 5.2, p.10: all reported experiments run on a classical-computer simulator. The platform-limitation reason is the authors' statement of why, and is carried as theirs.
egoqgnn-experiment-setup-ulayers-optimiz: Section 5.2, p.9-10: three Ulayers, identical structure, no shared parameters; one qubit per scalar node feature; UOBYQA derivative-free optimizer.
egoqgnn-experiment-hardware-and-datasets: Sections 5 to 5.3, p.8-10: six benchmarks (MUTAG, four PTC, PROTEINS), Intel Xeon E3-1270 v5 with 32GB for all methods, mean and std of 10-fold accuracy.
egoqgnn-baseline-sources-and-reruns: Section 5.2, p.10: deep-learning baseline numbers mostly from [25], [22]; 10-fold reruns for GIN, DGCNN on PTC FM/MM/FR and R-GCN, edGNN on PROTEINS.
egoqgnn-quantum-baseline-inputs: Sections 5.1-5.2, p.9-10: 8-dimensional graphlet vector for QSVM and QCNN; PCA to 3 dimensions for QSVM.
egoqgnn-simulator-setup: Section 5.2, p.10: 'implemented using the OriginQ simulator on a classical computer'; all experiments run on a simulator.
ai-nodes-edges-frequencies-scope: Abstract, p.1: states the paper designs frequencies for single- and two-qubit gates (node and edge parameters) together.
ai-graph-mapping-definition: Algorithm section, p.2: each node is a qubit, each edge a directly coupled pair.
ai-localization-assumption: Introduction, p.1: the localization assumption is stated as an assumption, and the evaluator is trained on small circuits because of it. Supplement Sec. I.A adds exponential decay with distance (Fig. S1b) as its support.
ai-evaluator-dataset-sizes: Results of the evaluator, p.3: 61,440 training, 12,800 testing or validation, about 1,000 on larger graphs. Matches the supplement's split (80/10/10 of 76,800 and 10% of 128,000).
ai-evaluator-log-targets-and-error-clip: Results of the evaluator, p.3, and Supplement II.D: base-10 log targets; errors below 1e-4 ignored; errors above 1e-1 capped at 1e-1.
ai-evaluator-mlp-architecture: Results of the evaluator, p.3 (one MLP per operation type) and Supplement Sec. I.A: each MLP has 4 hidden layers of 32 neurons.
ai-designer-default-error-weights: Results of the designer, p.4, Eq. 2: default weights wX = wY = wXY = 1.
ai-designer-training-setup: Results of the designer, p.4: training graphs of about 54, 103, 218 nodes, batch 288, about 700,000 steps, about 2 days on an RTX 4090.
ai-designer-medium-training-size-stateme: Introduction, p.1-2: medium-scale training with about 100 qubits, application to nearly 1000 qubits. Faithful to the Introduction; the training graphs in Results are 54, 103 and 218 nodes.
ai-test-set-and-compared-methods: Results of the designer, p.4: 30 x 6 random graphs with average qubit numbers 32, 54, 103, 218, 450, 870; three comparison methods named.
ai-large-scale-only-gnn-and-snake: Supplement Sec. I.C: the GNN designer and Snake are the only two run on large graphs; the others are limited to medium-scale graphs, as stated.
ai-baseline-settings-powell-scope-4: Supplement Sec. I.C: Powell optimizer with Scipy defaults for Snake and DirectOptim; Snake scope 4.
ai-numerical-simulation-instead-of-exper: Introduction p.2 and Results p.4: errors are modeled by numerical simulation, not real experiments, and all methods use the same trained evaluator. The 'possible because crosstalk exists in ideal systems' clause is the authors' rationale.
ai-three-order-gcn-rationale: Supplement Sec. I.B: three-order GCN chosen, with the authors' stated reason (errors relate mainly to up-to-3-hop neighbors, Fig. S1b). The design choice is setup; the reason is carried as theirs.
ai-designer-network-sizes: Supplement Sec. I.B: node GCN with 12 hidden layers, mostly 256 neurons; edge GCN with 3 hidden layers of 64 neurons.
ai-edge-frequency-as-node-mixture: Supplement Sec. I.B, Eq. 2 and Fig. S1: edge frequency equals pi*wi + pj*wj, with preferences from an MLP and softmax.
ai-designer-batched-use-batch-sizes: Supplement Sec. I.B: five qubit sizes listed with six batch sizes (512, 512, 512, 64, 8, 2). The paper's own text lists five sizes against six batch sizes; the value copies this faithfully.
ai-crosstalk-and-operations-definition: Demonstration, p.3: crosstalk definition; three operations RX, RY for nodes and RXY for edges.
ai-simulation-parameters: Supplement Sec. II.D: 4.9 to 5.1 GHz, coupler about 6.0 GHz on the ZZ-free line, anharmonicity 300 MHz, couplings 10 and 100 MHz, driving 25 MHz, residual 0.1 and 0.01 MHz.
ai-zz-free-line-operating-assumption: Supplement Sec. II.A: the paper states that the two couplings cannot both be zero and that it holds the coupler on the ZZ-free line, leaving XY crosstalk to the frequency design.
ai-time-duration-averaging: Supplement Sec. II.C and II.D: 20 durations sampled from 0 to 2pi/Omega_x; errors averaged. The text also averages over two initial states (40 cases); the value is not wrong.
ai-fixed-coupling-and-driving-strengths: Supplement Sec. II.C item 3: coupling and driving strengths are fixed, not designed. The 'decreasing helps' clause is a general statement cited to [12] and used as the authors' reason; the scope is the fixed values.
ai-classical-error-sources-excluded: Supplement Sec. II.C: classical error sources are not considered, with the stated reason that they are usually graph-independent.
ai-evaluator-dataset-generation: Supplement Sec. II.D: 25,600 samples per operation type on each 6-qubit graph, 128,000 in total over five graphs.
ai-evaluator-split-and-generalization-te: Supplement Sec. II.D: 3 training graphs split 80/10/10; 2 graphs held out for new-structure tests; about 1,000 points on a 30-qubit chain.
ai-future-error-sources: Discussion, p.4: the authors state that other error sources, qubit variation and experimental training data are left for future work. It states what the present evaluator does not cover.
ai-three-stair-setup: Abstract, p.1 and Fig. 1 / Algorithm section, p.2-3: evaluator trained on small circuits for medium ones; designer trained on medium circuits for large ones; crosstalk as the demonstration.
ts-teacher-label-generation: Section 4.1, p.4: grid inputs in [-pi, pi], several random processing-gate initializations, ancilla measurement as the label.
ts-angle-encoding-and-processing-gates: Section 3, p.3: U(x) = Rx(x1) x Rx(x2) on two qubits (angle encoding), same for all models; processing gates Rot and CZ.
ts-label-measurement-setup: Section 3, p.3, Eq. 1: one qubit measured in Z, cost is the squared difference, minimized in training.
ts-qp-hidden-perceptron-deferred-measure: Section 3.1, p.3-4: the hidden perceptron is defined as a processing gate, a controlled-NOT onto an ancilla, and a deferred measurement. The 'idea' that this gives non-linearity is stated as an idea; Section 6 finds it insufficient when outputs are reused.
ts-qp-uses-angle-encoding-continuous: Section 3.1, p.4: the paper uses angle encoding in place of the cited basis encoding, which allows continuous inputs and weights. The basis-encoding remark about refs [1], [30] is a cited description.
ts-ru-definition: Section 3.2, p.4: each data unitary followed by a trainable unitary; Li = U(w)U(x) repeated. Re-uploading is the term the paper uses.
ts-ru-same-readout-and-cost-as-qp: Section 3.2, p.4: the RU uses a multi-controlled NOT onto an ancilla like the QP and the same cost (Eq. 1).
ts-relative-entropy-definition: Section 4.2, p.4-5, Eq. 2: KL divergence between offset and normalized prediction maps, averaged over teacher-student pairs.
ts-accuracy-and-loss-metrics-definition: Section 4.2, p.5: accuracy is the share of correct binary labels. The 'all tools should be taken into account' clause is the authors' protocol stance, carried as theirs.
ts-deep-teacher-setup: Section 5.2, p.6, Fig. 3: a re-uploading teacher with four pairs of encoding gates; the QP and RU students have one and two pairs.
ts-encoding-comparison-setup: Section 5.4, p.7-8: compares angle encoding with Rot(x1,x2,0)H, using 500 points from the circular data set, probability vectors and PCA to 2D, without processing gates.
ts-open-question-coherent-deep-qnn: Section 6, p.8: after the experiments (Fig. 4b, 4c) the authors state that building deep QNNs coherently with end-only measurement remains open. The one-to-one mapping clause is their inference.
ts-simulation-pennylane-setup: Section 8, p.8: 'The simulations were made with the Pennylane library [39]'.
ts-aim-setup: Abstract, p.1: the aim is the teacher-student scheme for comparing QNN architectures. It states what the paper sets out to cover; it is not a claim that the scheme succeeded.
black-box-model-queries-as-time: Section 3.1, p.265: black-box model; complexity counted in oracle queries, called time.
distance-assumptions-minimal: Section 3.1, p.265: distance non-negative with Dist(xi,xi)=0; no triangle inequality; symmetry assumed for simplicity.
black-box-not-realistic-qram-pointer: Section 3.1, p.266: the authors state the black-box assumption is not realistic and point to QRAM of Giovannetti et al. as a route.
qram-adjacency-matrix-needs-quadratic-ti: Section 4, p.270: the authors argue that storing the full adjacency matrix costs at least Omega(n^2) (each entry read once), no better than Prim. A short argument, stated as a limit of the speed-up.
median-definition-medoid: Section 3.2, p.268, Definition 1: median of a set as a point with minimal summed distance; medoid note.
approximate-median-brassard-2011-not-ass: Section 3.2, p.268: the authors state they leave the effect of approximate medians on clustering quality for further research.
k-medians-np-hard-no-exact-quantum: Section 6.1, p.273: the authors state their quantum k-medians is a quantized heuristic, not an exact algorithm. The NP-hardness fact is cited (Papadimitriou 1981); the limit on their own algorithm is theirs.
k-medians-iteration-count-unchanged: Section 6.1, p.274: the authors state the quantum version does not change the number of iterations t, and leave any speed-up of t to future work.
distributed-setup-two-parties: Section 6.2, p.274-275: two participants, finite attribute precision, n points shared equally.
neighbourhood-graph-definition: Section 7.1, p.278, Definition 8: the complete distance-weighted graph reduced to each vertex's k closest neighbours.
quantized-kdtree-case-no-advantage: Section 8.1, p.282: the authors state that quantizing the distance-only algorithm gives no significant advantage over classical kd-trees when d is small. A caveat on their own neighbourhood-graph speed-up (citing Kibriya and Frank 2007).
max-min-initialization-definition: Section 7.3, p.281: the max-min type initialization (centre with maximum summed distance to previous centres) that Algorithm 8 quantizes, defined formally for the paper's use.
neighbourhood-outlier-lower-bound-open: Section 8.1, p.283: the authors state the true lower bound is only conjectured ('seems likely'), so optimality of their neighbourhood-graph and outlier algorithms is not established. The conjecture itself is an intuition, not a result.
k-medians-bound-gap-open: Section 8.1, p.283: the authors state a gap remains between the lower and upper bound for quantum k-medians.
open-question-lower-bounds-clustering: Section 8.1, p.282: the authors state lower bounds against all classical algorithms are an open question; they do not claim such a separation.

theory_low.egoqgnn-lemma1-tensor-product-injective: Lemma 1, Section 4.1, p.5. The statement is not an injectivity claim as worded (it excludes linearly dependent vectors). The Appendix proof (p.11-12) is a sketch for real scalars. Not a clean proved result.
theory_low.egoqgnn-lemma3-distinct-nodes-distinct-s: Lemma 3, p.5; Appendix p.12. The same-neighbor-count case concludes inequality from Lemmas 1 and 2 but never uses node features or neighborhoods. The proof is incomplete.
theory_low.egoqgnn-theorem1-distinguishes-gnn-nonis: Theorem 1, p.5; Appendix p.12 (labeled Theorem 4 there). Rests on Lemma 3, whose proof is incomplete. The step from unequal node states to unequal summed entropies is asserted with 'Moreover' and no argument.
theory_low.egoqgnn-theorem2-decomposition-equivalen: Theorem 2, Section 4.4, p.7. The text says the proof is in the Appendix, but the Appendix holds proofs only of Lemmas 1 to 3 and the isomorphism theorem. No proof of Theorem 2 is in the paper text.
theory_low.egoqgnn-parameter-example-32-dimension: Section 5.3.4, p.10. An illustrative count (1024 against 15 parameters) offered as a possible reason for fewer parameters. It is the authors' argument, not a proved result or a measurement.
theory_low.ai-theory-inspired-evaluator-lorentzian: Supplement Sec. III: the Lorentzian form is the authors' theoretical expectation ('suggesting', 'expected'), used as a fit with learnable parameters. Not derived or proved in the paper.
theory_low.quant-find-max-farthest-pair-linear: Theorem 1, Section 3.2, p.267 and Section 5, p.271. The proof is one sentence pointing to the analysis of Durr and Hoyer (1996). Proved elsewhere, cited. The theorem text is partly garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.classical-median-quadratic-lower-bound: Section 3.2, p.268: the Omega(n^2) classical bound comes from an informal adversarial scenario, not a formal proof. 'Most efficient possible' is argued by example.
theory_low.quant-find-median-lemma-1: Lemma 1, p.269. The proof is a two-line composition: O(sqrt n) uses of Durr-Hoyer minimum finding (cited) times an O(n) distance-sum circuit. The success probability is not argued beyond the cited result. The text layer is partly garbled.
theory_low.k-clustering-max-spacing-quantum-n32: Section 4, p.270: follows from Theorem 3, which is Durr et al. (2004), cited. Proved elsewhere; the paper only applies it, on the stated oracle-cost condition.
theory_low.divisive-clustering-quantum-gain: Theorem 4, Section 5, p.271-272. The value drops the gain expression, so the claim is vague. The proof covers a balanced and an unbalanced case and uses an informal classical Omega(n^2) farthest-pair bound; the 'all cases' claim is not shown for intermediate splits.
theory_low.quantum-k-medians-theorem-5: Theorem 5, Section 6.1, p.273-274. The value drops the gain expression. The proof treats only two extremes (equal-size clusters, one huge cluster) and uses the informal classical median bound; it asserts 'all cases'.
theory_low.distributed-trivial-protocol-cost: Section 6.2, p.274: a short remark about the trivial protocol's cost, no proof. The Theta(dm) and Theta(dn) figures are the authors' simple argument.
theory_low.distributed-grover-iteration-lemma-2: Lemma 2, Section 6.2, p.276. The proof is a description of the protocol steps (only steps 3 and 6 communicate). A sketch, not a derivation of the cost.
theory_low.distributed-k-medians-theorem-6: Theorem 6, Section 6.2, p.276-278. The proof treats two extremes only and asserts the balanced case is worst. The statement is garbled in the text layer (radical sign lost).
theory_low.quantum-neighbourhood-graph-theorem-7: Theorem 7, Section 7.1, p.279. The proof multiplies n by the cost of the cited quant_find_smallest_values (Durr et al. 2004). The 'with high probability' over n calls is not argued. Rests on a cited result.
theory_low.quantum-outlier-detection-theorem-8: Theorem 8, Section 7.2, p.280-281. The proof reuses Theorem 7 and adds an O(kn) step. 'Identifies all the outliers' depends on an empirically chosen threshold; the classical Omega(n^2) claim is stated with no proof.
theory_low.quantum-initialization-theorem-9: Theorem 9, Section 7.3, p.281. The value gives no bound and the statement is garbled in the text layer. The proof is a sum of cited-subroutine costs (quant_find_max).

requote.hqnn-qcnn-scalability-limit: regraded LOW at the team lead's decision: Section 2.2, p.4: a general statement about QCNN under NISQ limits, in the model description. Not a limit the paper shows or states about its own results. A field statement.

value_replace.hqnn-qcnn-scalability-limit: The authors state that, given the limitations of current NISQ devices, the QCNN can only handle a small number of qubits, limiting its scalability.

hqnn-qcnn-scalability-limit: However, given the limitations of current NISQ devices, the QCNN can only handle a small number of qubits, limiting its scalability.
